approved: Commonwealth Electoral Amendment (Cleaning up Political Donations) Bill 2023
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would tighten rules on political donations by lowering the disclosure threshold, capping donations, and banning contributions from certain industries.
Donors would be limited to $50,000 per electoral cycle, and recipients must report gifts over $1,000 to the Australian Electoral Commission within two business days.
The changes would start on the first day of the financial year after the 28th day following Royal Assent.
Lowers the donation disclosure threshold to $1,000 and requires aggregation of multiple gifts from the same source.
Expands the definition of a gift to include electoral spending, gifts-in-kind, and payments for fundraisers.
Introduces a $50,000 cap on total donations per donor during an electoral cycle.
Requires real-time disclosure of donations exceeding the threshold within two business days.
Prohibits donations from fossil fuel, gambling, liquor, and tobacco industry entities.
Increases penalties for corporations that break the law.
Political donors, recipients including parties, candidates, and associated entities, and the Australian Electoral Commission.

The member for Clark reintroduced the Commonwealth Electoral Amendment (Cleaning up Political Donations) Bill 2023, proposing to lower the donation disclosure threshold to $1,000, require real-time disclosure within two business days, ban donations from fossil fuel, gambling, liquor and tobacco companies, cap individual donations at $50,000 per electoral cycle, and cap campaign spending. The bill was seconded by the member for Mayo, who argued political donations must be reformed to improve public trust.
